free_text: The patient is a 71-year-old male with a PSA of 13.2 ng/mL and a prior diagnosis of ISUP grade group 2 prostate adenocarcinoma. MRI shows a PI-RADS 4 lesion (cT2a) in the peripheral zone, mid left, with restricted diffusion. The management assessment requires reviewing individual treatment benefit against the trade-off between active surveillance and treatment, given the documented grade and extent of disease.
